Machine Learning · IUCN + Environmental Data

AI-Based Extinction Risk Prediction

A random-forest model, trained on 168 species with IUCN assessments, estimates the probability that a species is threatened (CR, EN or VU) from its recorded range, climate niche, protection and land-use context. These are model predictions, not Red List assessments.

Extinction Cascade Simulator

The Web of Life

Two views of the same question. First, an illustrative food web you can disturb to see how losses travel. Then a scenario on real interactions documented in the Global Biotic Interactions database: remove a species and watch which dependent taxa could follow. Each run is a scenario, not a forecast.

Part 1 · Illustrative food webA teaching model of how a loss travels through a food web. Species and links are simplified, not computed from data.

Analytical Module · Species Richness

Record Concentration Zones

The nine 0.75° grid cells where occurrence records concentrate most, with the species observed and the share under wildlife protection. These are record concentration zones, not officially recognised biodiversity hotspots.

Chronicle of Conservation

India's Biodiversity Through the Ages

1972
Wildlife Protection Act — India's first comprehensive legal framework shielding endangered species and their habitats from exploitation.
1973
Project Tiger launched with nine reserves after the 1972 count found about 1,800 tigers. The 2022 estimate is about 3,680.
1992
Project Elephant launched to protect Asian elephants, their habitats and migration corridors.
2002
Biological Diversity Act — India's national legislation for conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of biological resources.
2009
Kaziranga's greater one-horned rhinoceros count passes 2,000, a recovery from near-extinction in the early twentieth century.
2011
The Great Indian Bustard is uplisted to Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List, as its population falls to a few hundred birds.
2022
Cheetahs are released in Kuno National Park, seventy years after the species was declared extinct in India.
2026
BioIndia brings 1.4 million GBIF records for 188 species across all 36 states and union territories into one open analysis platform.
Art & Natural History

India's Eternal Wildlife Heritage

India's painting traditions have long imagined forests and waters crowded with life. These illustrations echo that vision; conservation is the work of keeping it true.

The living forest — cranes, deer and flowering trees in an illustration inspired by Indian miniature painting.
The lotus pool — wetlands like this hold much of India's freshwater life, from mugger crocodiles to waterbirds.

Taxonomy · Distribution · Trends

Species Intelligence Pages

Browse a profile for every species with records — search by name or filter by group to see its distribution, recording trend, protection, climate and land use, model-predicted risk and documented ecological connections.

Longitudinal Analysis · 2000–2025

Time-Series Biodiversity Analysis

Records per year for the five flagship species, indexed to each species' peak year. Toggle species to compare. These trends track recording effort, not population size.

Climate · Deforestation · Urbanisation

Environmental Impact Analysis

The climate and land-use conditions where each flagship species is recorded — baseline temperature, rainfall and elevation, tree cover, recent forest loss and built-up land. These are associations, not causes.

SHAP Values · Feature Importance · Decision Trees

Explainable AI Insights

Transparent model explanations showing which environmental and biological variables most influence extinction risk predictions — making the AI scientifically accountable.
